title: US Readies New Tariffs on 16 Partners, India Included, as Soon as Tuesday
excerpt: Reuters reports the Section 301 excess-capacity findings could land Tuesday or Wednesday, with country-tailored duties proposed on top of existing tariffs — but no rates announced yet.
body:
• The Trump administration is expected to release findings of its Section 301 excess-capacity probe as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, with new import duties proposed on goods from 16 trading partners, according to Reuters.
  • India is one of the 16 partners investigated, alongside China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam and others.
  • No rates have been announced yet. One source told Reuters the White House is expected to honour deal caps of 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19% for Malaysia, and a 20% cap on second-term tariffs on China while its trade truce lasts.
  • For Indian exporters selling into the US, there is nothing to file or pay yet — the next step is the US Trade Representative's announcement, which will set out any proposed rates country by country.

The Trump administration is poised to release the findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected, Reuters reported, citing three people with knowledge of the matter.

The investigation was carried out under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The US Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump's second term, the people said.

Who is in the probe

USTR has been investigating what it called evidence of excess industrial capacity in most of the United States' largest trading partners: China, the European Union, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia.

USTR launched the excess capacity probe in March. A White & Case analysis of the initiation notice said USTR alleged the economies "are producing more goods than they can consume domestically," which it said displaces US domestic production or prevents investment and expansion in US manufacturing. The notice listed sectors including aluminium, automobiles, batteries, chemicals, electronics, semiconductors, solar modules and steel.

What is known about the rates — and what is not

It was unclear what tariff rates would be proposed, or what exemptions may be granted, Reuters reported. One of the people said the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies.

The same person said the White House is expected to honour capped tariff rates included in finalised US trade deals — duty caps of 15% on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea, and 19% for Malaysia. No equivalent cap for India was reported by Reuters.

Ryan Majerus, a former senior Commerce Department trade official and a partner at King & Spalding, told Reuters he expects a lengthy report that could include differentiated tariff remedies for each of the 16 trading partners, and that the administration could propose tariff rates of 15% to 25% on imports from countries deemed to have excess capacity in various sectors. Those figures are Majerus's expectation, not an announced rate.

China, the truce, and the tariffs these would partly replace

The administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity, which it says is flooding global markets with steel, aluminium, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. China has rejected the accusations, saying its exports reflect competitive advantages, Reuters reported. The probe is also partly directed at Chinese investment in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia, to manufacture goods for the US market and avoid tariffs.

Under a US-China trade truce due to expire on January 10, the administration has capped second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, in addition to duties of about 25% imposed during Trump's first term. One of the people told Reuters the 20% cap would likely be maintained as long as the truce is extended; if it expires, the excess capacity rate would rise to a higher level.

The new duties would partly replace global import taxes struck down by the US Supreme Court in February, Reuters reported. USTR and the White House did not immediately respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement.

What to watch next

The findings themselves are the next step. Until USTR publishes proposed rates, no new duty is in force under this probe, and importers cannot yet calculate a country-specific cost from it. The announcement, expected as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, is what will show whether India faces a proposed rate, at what level, and on which goods.
